content: Certainly. 1. Ethinyl estradiol and exenatide injectable solution should be used with caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide’s effect of slowing gastric emptying may decrease the absorption and efficacy of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should be advised to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. 2. Ethinyl estradiol and exenatide injectable suspension require careful monitoring. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Exenatide’s delayed gastric emptying effect may reduce the absorption of oral medications. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide. 3. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 4. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments of finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 5. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects from flibanserin. 6. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Ethinyl estradiol doses should not exceed 30 mcg/day. 9. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Ethinyl estradiol increases green tea levels by reducing its elimination. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce hemin efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase. Estrogens in high systemic doses may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 16. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin detemir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 18. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin glargine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 19. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin glulisine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 20. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 22. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin NPH through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 23. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 24. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, especially at higher istradefylline doses. 26. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Ethinyl estradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma lamotrigine concentrations, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 31. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions for CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 35. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. GLP-1 agonists delay gastric emptying, which may affect the absorption of oral medications. 36. Ethinyl estradiol increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Ethinyl estradiol increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Ethinyl estradiol increases midazolam levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This may prolong sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraceptive methods are recommended. 45. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Mitotane decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 47. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions for BCRP substrates. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 48. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Nafcillin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Nemolizumab decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, potentially increasing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for decreased systemic levels of sensitive CYP substrates. Dosage modification may be needed. 51. Neomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 52. Ethinyl estradiol increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Ethinyl estradiol increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Nirmatrelvir decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing metabolism, possibly through ritonavir-mediated CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for the remainder of the cycle. 55. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Ethinyl estradiol increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 60. Penicillin G aqueous decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing metabolism. There is a risk of oral contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Penicillin VK decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised.
